evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Papavasiliou and Schatz, 2002 and Lefranc and Lefranc, 2020.

claim: Over half of AIRR-seq survey respondents currently already use controls (mostly of a homebrew variety) in their experiments.
source: There is broad agreement that controls and standards are desirable, with over half of AIRR-seq survey respondents currently already using controls (mostly of a homebrew variety) in their experiments.
evidence: The claim is based on data from the survey described in the manuscript.

claim: Survey respondents agree on the types of issues in analyzing and interpreting AIRR-seq data that would benefit from the use of controls - most importantly measuring and controlling for sample quality, assay sensitivity and specificity, and calibration for the quantification of clonal size.
source: Furthermore, whether individuals used controls or did not, they appeared to agree on the types of issues in analyzing and interpreting AIRR-seq data that would benefit from the use of controls - most importantly measuring and controlling for sample quality, assay sensitivity and specificity, and calibration for the quantification of clonal size.
evidence: The claim is based on data from the survey described in the manuscript.

claim: It is unlikely that a single control can fulfill all needs across all methods and applications in AIRR-seq.
source: It is unlikely that a single control can fulfill all of these needs across all methods and applications.
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the text as a conclusion drawn from the discussion of diverse AIRR-seq methods and needs.

claim: There is at the moment no obvious front-runner for a 'gold standard' that can be used to judge the adequacy of different types of controls in AIRR-seq.
source: There is at the moment also no obvious front-runner for a 'gold standard' that can be used to judge the adequacy of different types of controls.
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the text as an observation about the current state of the field.

claim: The AIRR Community Biological Resources WG plans to focus on three forms of controls: one in-parallel (synthetic standards), one in-parallel and computational (UMIs), and one that is external (a complex cell mixture).
source: Based upon the current use of controls and needs identified by our survey respondents, the WG plans to focus on three forms of controls: one in-parallel (synthetic standards), one in-parallel and computational (UMIs), and one that is external (a complex cell mixture that is run in parallel to monitor amplification and sequencing run batch effects).
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the text as a description of the WG's plans.

claim: The WG proposes to carry out a multi-center analysis of three types of controls: (1) synthetic calibrators for bulk gDNA sequencing, (2) UMIs for samples studied in parallel by bulk mRNA and single cell sequencing, and (3) a mixed cell population for the evaluation of batch effects.
source: We therefore propose to carry out a multi-center analysis of three types of controls: (1) synthetic calibrators for bulk gDNA sequencing to measure clonal size and amplification bias; (2) UMIs for samples studied in parallel by bulk mRNA (with UMIs) and single cell sequencing (with cellular barcodes) for the analysis of amplification bias and sequencing error; and (3) a mixed cell population (either a human apheresis and/or pooled tissue product or murine spleen samples) for the evaluation of batch effects that compare between sequencing runs performed at the same site or between runs performed at different sites.
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the text as a description of the WG's proposed work.

claim: Spleen cells are enriched for memory B-cell clones and are useful for modeling clonal expansion and somatic hypermutation.
source: Spleen cells are enriched for memory B-cell clones and are useful for modeling clonal expansion and somatic hypermutation (Meng et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Meng et al., 2017.

claim: The literature reflects increasing use of single-cell approaches in AIRR-seq.
source: Altogether, these initial results suggest that among survey respondents bulk sequencing on mRNA and gDNA are the most frequently used methods. However, the literature reflects increasing use of single-cell approaches, including the computational construction of IG or TR from RNA-sequencing (RNA-seq) libraries (Figure 2—figure supplement 1) and the combined use of target capture plus single-cell RNA-seq (e.g., 10X Genomics' 5′ end kits, etc.).
